description: The GCP-CEM (Global Carbon Project Cement-Process Emissions) dataset provides globally consistent estimates of CO₂ emissions from the cement production process—specifically those arising from carbonate decomposition during clinker production, excluding fossil fuel combustion emissions. The dataset spans 1880–2024, covering virtually all cement-producing countries, and is updated regularly to incorporate UNFCCC reports, national inventories, and USGS data. Cement and clinker production data are compiled from official national sources, UNFCCC Common Reporting Format files, and alternative datasets (e.g., CDIAC, USGS, GNR), with meticulous source tracking for each data point. Emissions are calculated using country-specific or IPCC default emission factors, adjusted where national data are available. The dataset integrates recent transparency and biennial reports, corrections to historical data, and enhanced coverage for countries such as Egypt, Indonesia, and Iran. It forms a key input to major global datasets, including the Global Carbon Budget, PRIMAP-hist, and CEDS. Overall, GCP-CEM offers a comprehensive, historically extended, and methodologically transparent record of process-based cement CO₂ emissions—an essential resource for climate modeling, carbon accounting, and long-term emissions analysis.
